title: Height-Balanced Glyph Retrieval and Rendering in a C++ JIT Bitmap Engine for Microcontrollers
topic: JIT bitmap text rendering for microcontrollers
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: This paper presents a lightweight JIT bitmap text rendering engine tailored for microcontrollers. The engine stores glyphs in a height-balanced binary search tree, enabling $O(\log N)$ lookup and insertion while preserving strict key order and height balance. Rendering proceeds by traversing the tree to fetch glyph bitmaps and composing them into a framebuffer with per-pixel clipping. We formally prove that the tree invariant guarantees bounded search depth and that the rendering loop respects spatial memory hierarchy constraints. No empirical timing data is reported; instead, we provide static analysis of the source AST and asymptotic complexity bounds. The implementation is available in C++ and is fully reproducible from the public repository. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/cpp-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261108_170304_jit_bitmap_text_rendering_for}
